comparison: Both address literature-based contextual claims (C103-C152). OpenEval categorizes these as SUPPORTED background information, while peer reviewers note the authors 'have presented logical support for their conclusions' and do not challenge these contextual claims. High agreement on the validity of literature citations.

Both address ECM-mediated sEV secretion (C1-C6 in OpenEval; C1-C13 in peer review). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers agree, noting 'a more concrete link between fibronectin and the secretion of extracellular vesicles' with 'largely solid' data and 'mostly convincing' evidence.

OpenEval addresses SMPD3 mechanism (C7-C9) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R1 includes these claims in broader assessment of fibronectin-sEV link. Both find evidence convincing, though peer reviewers note 'some limitations' in vesicle origin assessment.

OpenEval addresses integrin/FAK/Src signaling (C10-C13) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R1 includes these in overall positive assessment of fibronectin-integrin signaling pathway. Both evaluations agree on the strength of the mechanistic evidence.

OpenEval addresses actin inhibitor effects (C14-C16) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R2 covers broader actin cytoskeleton claims (C14-C29) but rates them UNCERTAIN, noting 'limitations' in 'assessment of vesicle origins, contents and their association with the actin cytoskeleton.' Disagreement on completeness of mechanistic resolution.

OpenEval addresses F-actin/cortactin/CD63 colocalization (C17-C22) as SUPPORTED despite noting 'rare events' in live imaging. Peer review R2 rates these claims UNCERTAIN due to 'limitations' in actin cytoskeleton assessment. Peer reviewers are more cautious about mechanistic conclusions.

OpenEval addresses filopodia-mediated transport (C23-C25) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R2 includes these in UNCERTAIN evaluation of actin-related claims. OpenEval acknowledges limitations but finds evidence sufficient; peer reviewers want stronger mechanistic proof.

OpenEval addresses MVB docking and filopodia hypothesis (C26-C29) as SUPPORTED but notes C28-C29 are 'more speculative' with 'acknowledged limitations.' Peer review R2 rates overlapping claims UNCERTAIN. Both recognize speculative nature, with peer reviewers more conservative.

OpenEval explicitly categorizes C28-C29 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are 'speculative or requiring further study.' Peer review R2 rates broader actin-related claims UNCERTAIN. Agreement that these specific filopodia mechanism claims need more evidence.

OpenEval addresses ECM trapping of sEVs (C30-C33) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R3 covers broader sEV-ECM interactions (C31-C47) as SUPPORTED, noting 'robust imaging data' as a strength. Strong agreement on ECM trapping evidence.

OpenEval addresses sequential extraction and EV populations (C34-C36) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R3 includes these in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of sEV-ECM interactions with 'robust imaging data.' Agreement on methodology and findings.

OpenEval addresses FN trafficking and cell density effects (C37-C43) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R3 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation of sEV-ECM interactions. Both find the correlation between FN trafficking and sEV secretion convincing.

OpenEval addresses FN as sEV cargo (C44-C45) as SUPPORTED by western blot and flow cytometry. Peer review R3 includes these in broader SUPPORTED evaluation. Agreement on FN as bona fide sEV cargo protein.

OpenEval addresses differential sEV behavior (C46-C47) as SUPPORTED by super-resolution microscopy. Peer review R3 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation with 'robust imaging data.' Agreement on functional insights from ECM trapping.

OpenEval addresses proteomic analysis of atherosclerotic plaques (C48-C53) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R4 covers broader plaque findings (C48-C61) as SUPPORTED, noting 'nice validation of in vitro findings in diseased human cohort.' Strong agreement on proteomic evidence.

OpenEval addresses sEV accumulation in plaques (C54-C58) as SUPPORTED by immunofluorescence and colocalization analysis. Peer review R4 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation highlighting 'inclusion of human-derived samples' as strength. Agreement on in vivo validation.

OpenEval addresses circulating FN as source (C59-C61) as SUPPORTED but notes 'lack of shown RT-PCR data is a limitation.' Peer review R4 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation. Both find conclusion reasonable despite data presentation limitations.

OpenEval addresses 2D migration effects (C62-C65) as SUPPORTED, noting sEVs have 'nuanced role' beyond speed. Peer review R5 covers migration claims (C62-C69) as SUPPORTED with 'largely solid' data. Agreement on migration findings.

OpenEval addresses 3D invasion directionality (C66-C69) as SUPPORTED, calling it 'novel and important finding.' Peer review R5 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation noting 'interesting cell autonomous pathway.' Strong agreement on directional effects.

OpenEval categorizes C65 as UNCERTAIN, noting it is 'speculative or requiring further study.' Peer review R5 rates broader migration claims SUPPORTED. Minor disagreement on strength of inference about sEV baseline effects.

OpenEval addresses adhesion and spreading effects (C70-C75) as SUPPORTED by multiple assays. Peer review R6 covers broader adhesion/FA claims (C70-C83) as SUPPORTED with 'wide range of assays' and 'largely solid' data. Agreement on adhesion inhibition.

OpenEval addresses FA dynamics and traction forces (C76-C83) as SUPPORTED by comprehensive measurements. Peer review R6 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation noting 'robust' FA analysis data. Strong agreement on mechanistic evidence for adhesion modulation.

OpenEval addresses sEV proteomic signature (C84-C89) as SUPPORTED by proteomic analysis and GO pathways. Peer review R7 covers broader proteomic claims (C84-C96) as SUPPORTED with 'largely solid' data. Agreement on adhesion-related protein signature.

OpenEval addresses collagen VI identification (C90-C93) as SUPPORTED by proteomics and western blot. Peer review R7 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation. Agreement on collagen VI as key sEV cargo with adhesion roles.

OpenEval addresses collagen VI localization (C94-C96) as SUPPORTED by dot-blot with/without permeabilization. Peer review R7 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation. Agreement on surface-exposed collagen VI finding.

OpenEval addresses collagen VI functional role (C97-C99) as SUPPORTED by antibody blocking and siRNA knockdown. Peer review R8 covers broader collagen VI claims (C97-C102) as SUPPORTED, noting 'nice validation' of in vitro findings. Strong agreement on functional evidence.

OpenEval addresses collagen VI expression in plaques (C100-C101) as SUPPORTED by RT-qPCR. Peer review R8 includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation providing 'nice validation' in human samples. Agreement on in vivo relevance.

OpenEval addresses main study conclusions (C102, C104, C106, C111, C113, C153) as SUPPORTED by converging evidence, noting 'some aspects remain to be fully elucidated.' Peer review R9 covers overlapping conclusions (C104, C111, C140, C146, C148, C151, C153) as SUPPORTED, noting 'authors largely achieved their aims' with 'mostly convincing' evidence. Agreement on overall model with acknowledged limitations.

OpenEval categorizes C124 as UNCERTAIN, noting 'data are not shown' making evaluation difficult. Peer review R10 includes C124 in broader SUPPORTED contextual claims. Disagreement stems from OpenEval's stricter requirement for shown data versus peer acceptance of mentioned observations.
